title: Pilot scoping — Sensitive inputs & benchmark sprint planning
next_steps: Maya to share pilot statement of work and pricing - 2026-03-20
Liam to provide benchmark config and workload scripts - 2026-03-22
Customer to provide 1 week of representative traffic and 200 sample prompts for redaction tests - 2026-03-24
Schedule kickoff for infra setup (VPC peering) - proposed 2026-03-25
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pilot SOW + pricing + security FAQ - due 2026-03-20
Liam O'Connor - Share bench harness (k6 + tokenized workloads) and runbook - due 2026-03-22
Samir Khan - Provide list of regulated fields to redact and sample PHI/PII tokens - due 2026-03-24
Tony Wu - Confirm VPC networking constraints and provide egress IP allowlist - due 2026-03-24
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-18 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jared Patel (Orchid Head of ML), Ana Ruiz (PM), Samir Khan (Security), Leah Park (Privacy), Tony Wu (Infra)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 3-week pilot focused on sensitive input handling and performance benchmarks. Agreed success criteria: redaction/regression tests pass, throughput & latency targets met for two core workloads, and no data residency or encryption blockers. Plan: Redwood to provision test endpoints (hosted with private VPC peering option), run bench harness, and iterate on redaction rules. Timeline: infra setup week 1, benchmarking week 2, analysis & exec review week 3.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we'll do a short agenda: define success criteria, confirm workloads for benchmarking, and the pilot timeline. Liam and I will cover the bench plan and the data handling options.
[00:27] Jared Patel: Sounds good. we're most worried about PII leaking into logs, and also cost. we have roughly 3k daily chat interactions in prod but those are expected to double. For the pilot we can do a 24h representative dump and a synthetic replay.
[00:44] Ana Ruiz: And from a PM side, we need to validate that user-facing latencies don't regress. goal is parity with our current microservice pipeline, ideally 95th < 800ms for short queries.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Okay noted. quick question about current infra, Tony? are you on EKS in AWS and do you have a private subnet we can peer to?
[01:18] Tony Wu: yes EKS, private subnets, nat gateways, we can do VPC peering. we'll need a list of egress IPs for the allowlist and any specific ports. also SOC2 compliance is required so we need audit logs preserved.
[01:36] Maya Chen: Redwood can do hosted endpoints with VPC peering and we also support Private deployment if you need an air-gapped option. for the host-with-peering mode logs can be ephemeral or persisted to your S3 via encrypted pipe depending on policy.
[01:55] Samir Khan: Important: logs must strip PII fields before persistence. we also need KMS-managed keys for any stored prompt material. can you support customer-managed keys?
[02:08] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; we can use your keys for at-rest encryption. Regarding PII, we provide a redaction hook in the runtime: configurable rules (regex + ML-based detection) that redact before disk. worth noting ML-detection is probabilistic so we recommend rule-based for high-confidence fields (SSN, credit card).
[02:36] Leah Park: Also asking: how long will prompt-level telemetry be retained? regulatory wants minimal retention for auditability but not full conversation history.
[02:47] Maya Chen: You can choose retention windows. Common options are ephemeral (7 days), short-term (30/90 days), or long-term (365). For this pilot we suggest ephemeral logs for PII-containing flows and a 30-day window for general telemetry so we can run regressions.
[03:08] Jared Patel: For success criteria, let's capture it now: 1) redaction tests must remove or mask 100% of test PII tokens in bench runs, 2) throughput: sustain 50 req/s with 1k token avg without 95th latency > 1.2s for summarization flows and 95th < 800ms for short chat, 3) cost per 1k tokens must be under our internal threshold (we'll share number), 4) integration and key management meet compliance. Is that feasible?
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: Feasible. We'll run two benchmark classes: A) conversational short queries (avg 80 tokens) at 50 req/s, B) long-context summarization (avg 1k tokens) at lower concurrency to stress KV cache. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimate.
[04:07] Ana Ruiz: How do you handle prompt storage — do you store raw prompts by default? that's a blocker for us.
[04:16] Maya Chen: By default hosted endpoints keep telemetry but you can enable ephemeral prompt mode which retains only hashed fingerprints and minimal metadata for debugging. We also support encrypting persisted prompts with your KMS and optional redaction at ingestion. For strict privacy, we can configure redaction to run client-side prior to send or use a proxy that strips tokens.
[04:38] Samir Khan: Client-side redaction increases our engineering effort. we'd prefer server-side if it's guaranteed. how confident is the redaction? do you have metrics?
[04:49] Liam O'Connor: We ran internal sims — rule-based redaction matches for structured PII types near 99.8% on known patterns; ML detectors catch obfuscated PII but with lower recall. For pilot we'll create a benchmark suite with 200 seeded PII samples you provide and measure false negatives/positives.
[05:11] Leah Park: Can you show an example of the persisted artifact after redaction? we need to see that no full SSNs or emails remain.
[05:20] Maya Chen: We'll include sample logs in the security FAQ. For the pilot we can send an anonymized log bundle post-redaction for review.
[05:30] Jared Patel: About retention: regulator says we must be able to retrieve logs for audits for up to 7 years but only after legal request; we want them off hot storage. can Redwood tier storing to cold S3?
[05:43] Maya Chen: Yes, we can configure lifecycle rules to move artifacts to cold storage encrypted with your KMS. Access controls and audit trails remain. For the pilot we'll keep only rolling short-term copies unless you specify otherwise.
[05:57] Tony Wu: Network question: if we do VPC peering with hosted endpoints will traffic egress through your NAT? we need to ensure data doesn't leave our VPC unencrypted.
[06:09] Liam O'Connor: Peered access keeps traffic within the AWS backbone; payload encryption in-flight is TLS and at-rest via your KMS. We'll share a network diagram.
[06:20] Ana Ruiz: Bench timing and timeline? you mentioned a 3-week sprint, can you spell out weeks?
[06:28] Maya Chen: Proposed: Week 1: infra setup, VPC peering, access + sample data ingestion + redaction rules configuration. Week 2: run benchmark harness across the two workloads, iterate on redaction rules and model variants. Week 3: analyze results, produce report, exec walkthrough and next-phase recommendation. We can compress to 2 weeks if infra is ready.
[06:53] Jared Patel: If we provide 24h replay and sample prompts, how long will bench runs take?
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: For 24h representative traffic replay at 50 req/s with controlled concurrency we'll run a 4-hour sustained test and a series of burst tests. Summarization workloads will be run as separate jobs, likely another 6 hours total. End-to-end runs including data collection ~1 day.
[07:18] Samir Khan: Security review: we need an architecture diagram and the SOC2 plus our CISO will want the SIEM integration notes.
[07:26] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2 report and a security checklist. We also include a sample SIEM forwarder for CloudWatch logs to your S3 or Splunk.
[07:36] Leah Park: On the redaction approach: can we run a strict mode that masks entire user messages if they contain high-risk tokens?
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: Yes — we support policy rules that either redact at field level or apply message-level suppression. For pilot we recommend field-level first, with fallback to suppression for high-risk categories.
[07:58] Tony Wu: What about model variants — do you run quantized models and does that impact hallucination or PII leakage?
[08:07] Liam O'Connor: Quantization and different kernels can change tokenization and subtle behavior. We'll include model-variant A/B tests: full-fp32 baseline vs quantized runtime. Quality metrics (BLEU-like or task-specific accuracy) will be tracked alongside latency.
[08:25] Ana Ruiz: Success criteria also needs a quality gate: less than 2% drop in classification accuracy on our labeled set.
[08:33] Jared Patel: Let's make that explicit: Quality drop <2% for critical intents, redaction false negatives <0.5% on seeded tests, and bench latency thresholds as earlier.
[08:46] Maya Chen: Noted, we'll document all thresholds in the SOW.
[08:51] Jared Patel: I want to surface procurement: any standard contract or is there an addendum for pilot?
[08:58] Maya Chen: We have a short pilot SOW and an addendum for security terms (DPA) that covers data handling. Pricing for the pilot is typically a capped usage number.
[09:08] Samir Khan: For KMS bring-your-own-key, can you confirm that Redwood never has access to the unwrapped keys?
[09:15] Liam O'Connor: Correct. With CMEK your service account only has permission to use the key through the KMS API, Redwood doesn't store the plaintext key. We can elaborate in the tech writeup.
[09:26] Ana Ruiz: Bench reporting: what format and dashboards?
[09:30] Liam O'Connor: We'll provide a perf dashboard (Grafana) with per-route token counts, p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and a CSV dump of raw traces for your analysis. We can also push a short summary deck.
[09:46] Jared Patel: For the seeded PII tests, we'll provide 200 samples across PHI/PII categories and expect a measured FN rate. If FN > 0.5% we fail the gate.
[09:58] Maya Chen: That's clear. we'll instrument the bench harness to flag any unredacted tokens and produce diffs.
[10:06] Leah Park: If we find unredacted content in persisted artifacts during the pilot, what's the rollback?
[10:12] Liam O'Connor: We can immediately suspend persistence and purge retained artifacts while we investigate. Also we'll keep audit logs of who accessed what.
[10:21] Tony Wu: On cost modelling: can you estimate per-token cost for the summarization runs if we pick a T4-like GPU vs A100?
[10:31] Liam O'Connor: We'll include cost estimates for model variants and hardware profiles. The bench run will include actual GPU hours so you get a realistic number.
[10:40] Jared Patel: Great. let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:44] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya will send SOW + security FAQ by 2026-03-20; Liam will share bench harness and initial config by 2026-03-22; Orchid to share sample prompts and PII seed list by 2026-03-24; Tony to confirm network allowlist and peering details by 2026-03-24; schedule infra kickoff for 2026-03-25 pending confirmations.
[11:10] Ana Ruiz: sounds good, thanks.
[11:12] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites.
[11:17] Jared Patel: Thanks all.
[47:00] [meeting end, recording stops]
